questions.stem: An 18-Year-old primigravida at 38 weeks gestation came to the OPD with chief complaints of leakage of fluid P/V. After examination, you’ve asked to perform a nitrazine test to find the presence of amniotic fluid in the vagina. All of the following will give a false positive test result, except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Scant fluid
  • Options A, B & C will give false positive results.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 435

questions.stem: A 23-Year-old primigravida presents to the ED in active labour at 6 cm dilation. Her membranes are intact, the fetus is in cephalic presentation, and the fetal tracing is a category I. Two hours later, she is still 4 cm dilated. She has her contractions every 6 minutes. Should the patient in this case achieve adequate uterine contractions for that, what is the minimum rate of cervical dilation in a woman?
questions.solutionHtml:
1- 2 cm/hr
  • Options B, C & D are false.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 439

questions.stemHtml: A 25-Year-old primigravida presents to the ED for induction of labour at 40 weeks gestation. On PV examination her cervix is unfavourable and it has a bishop score of 4. You manage the patient by giving them a drug of which, the chemical structure is depicted below. This agent belongs to which drug group?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prostaglandins

Options A, C & D are false.



William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 410

questions.stem: A 32-week G3P1A1 female presents with pain in the abdomen and contractions. She has no comorbidities. On examination, her pulse is 90 bpm, BP 124/72 mm Hg, temperature 98F and saturation 98%. She has a cephalic presentation with engaged head and abdominal distension appropriate for gestational age. Her prior USG reports are normal. She has abdominal contractions at the rate of 3 per 10 minutes. On PV examination, her os is dilated to about 3 cm and effaced. There is the presence of vaginal discharge. True about this condition are as followsMost common cause is idiopathicUterine anomalies and genital infections are commonly associatedSmoking is a protective factorMaternal stress can lead to this conditionHistory of previous abortion or spontaneous induction are the risk factors for this conditionSelect the correct answer from the given below code:-
questions.solutionHtml:
Option 3 is false
  • The given scenario is that of a preterm labour and smoking is a risk factor.
    All the other options are true.


DC Dutta’s, Textbook of Obstetrics, 8th Edition, Page No. 365

questions.stem: A 32-Year-old multigravida presents to the ED at 38 weeks of gestation at term and is admitted to the labour ward for further management and routine delivery care. She is conscious & oriented and on examination her vitals were normal and as time progresses, she goes into labour and after a few hours as she is in the active phase. On P/V examination the cervix becomes as thin as the adjacent lower uterine segment, what is the effacement seen in this case?
questions.solutionHtml:
100%
  • Options A, B & C are false.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 435

questions.stem: A 33-Year-old multigravida present in the labour ward in active labour at term. She progresses from 4 cm cervical dilation to completion within 3 hours. She delivers the baby spontaneously 30 minutes later. She has a third-degree perineal laceration that is repaired in the labour ward. The next day after delivery she is found to have urinary retention. What is her risk factor for urinary retention in the given patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Perineal laceration
  • Options A, B & D are false


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 438

questions.stem: A 37-Year-old multigravida presents for induction at 39 weeks gestation. The patient has a history of two prior vaginal deliveries, K.C.O. pre-gestational diabetes mellitus, chronic hypertension is on medications, and has a history of prior abruption in the setting of preeclampsia with moderate to severe features. You are the intern posted and you’re instructed by the obstetrician to place the patient on continuous fetal monitoring. How often should the tracing be evaluated?

options.label: A
options.text: Every 30 minutes in the first stage and every 15 minutes in the second stage

options.label: B
options.text: Every 15 minutes in the first stage and every 5 minutes in the second stage

options.label: C
options.text: Every 15 minutes in the first and second stage

options.label: D
options.text: Every 15 minutes in the first stage and every 30 minutes in the second stage

questions.answerText: Every 15 minutes in the first stage and every 5 minutes in the second stage
questions.solutionHtml:
Every 15 minutes in the first stage and every 5 minutes in the second stage
  • Options A, C & D are false. Since here the woman presents with multiple risk factors, hence the correct answer for the given case will be fetal heart auscultation is performed at least every 15 minutes during first-stage labour and every 5 minutes during the second stage.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 436

questions.stem: A primi patient was admitted to the labour room in early labour with thick meconium-stained liquor for which cardiotocography was done which is pathological. Following are the criteria of pathological CTG except for:

options.label: C
options.text: Single prolonged deceleration up to 3 min.

questions.answerText: Single prolonged deceleration up to 3 min.
questions.solutionHtml:
Single prolonged deceleration up to 3 min.

A single prolonged declaration of up to 3 mins is suspicious of a non-reassuring fetal heart rate. Options A, B & D are signs of pathological CTG.



Shaw’s Textbook of Gynaecology, 17th Edition, Page No. 71

questions.stem: All are true regarding Duncan's placental separation except

options.label: B
options.text: Maternal surface presents at the vulva

questions.solutionHtml:
Most common method of separation
  • Options A, B & C are true.


DC Dutta’s, Textbook of Obstetrics, 8th Edition, Page No. 144

questions.stem: The hormone responsible for decidual reaction and arias stella reaction in ectopic pregnancy is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Progesterone

Options A, C & D are false.



DC Dutta’s, Textbook of Obstetrics, 8th Edition, Page No. 210

questions.stemHtml: In the following curve below what stage is depicted by the letter C
questions.solutionHtml:
Phase of maximum slope
  • The pattern of cervical dilatation during the latent and active phases of normal labour is a sigmoid curve.
  • This curve is called the Friedman curve.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 435

questions.stemHtml: In the given image below, What is the fetal attitude?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sinciput
  • Options A, B & C are false. As shown in the above image the fetus in cephalic presentation with a deflexed head is in a sinciput attitude. Hence the correct answer is sinciput in attitude.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 422

questions.stemHtml: Mrs XYZ, 30 years, G3P2L2 with previous two LSCS with low-lying placenta at 34 weeks of gestation came into the outpatient department with ultrasound obstetrics which is suggestive of placenta accreta, so MRI was advised and done which shows all the findings given below except one:

options.label: B
options.text: Heterogeneous signal intensity within the placenta

options.label: D
options.text: Distance between uterine serosa bladder wall interface and the retroplacental vessels is 1 mm

questions.answerText: Distance between uterine serosa bladder wall interface and the retroplacental vessels is 1 mm
questions.solutionHtml:
Distance between uterine serosa bladder wall interface and the retroplacental vessels is < 1 mm
  • Is not seen in MRI, it is seen in USG with colour Doppler study. Options A, B & C are true.


DC Dutta’s, Textbook of Obstetrics, 8th Edition, Page No. 185

questions.stemHtml: What is the term used for the fetal asynclitism depicted in the drawing below?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior asynclitism

Options A, B & D are false.



William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 427

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions doesn’t cause any difficulty performing Leopold maneuvers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Large fetus
  • Options B, C & D can cause difficulties in performing Leopold maneuvers.


William Obstetrics, 25th Edition, Page No. 424
